title: Digamma as Bose kernel integral: psi(z) = Integral (e^{-t}/t - e^{-z t}/(1-e^{-t})) dt, Re z>0
expression_sketch: polygamma(0, z) - Integral(exp(-t)/t - exp(-z*t)/(1 - exp(-t)), (t, 0, oo))  ==  0
latent_structure: The Bose occupation kernel 1/(1-e^{-t}) is the integral master for psi on Re z>0. The combination e^{-t}/t - e^{-z t}/(1-e^{-t}) is integrable at t=0 (removable). This is the thermal generating representation of digamma, not a series of poles and not the Im-psi hyperbolic identities.

function_domains.polygamma: psi meromorphic; poles at nonpositive integers (DLMF 5.2.2); on Re z>0 those poles are absent

analytic_domains.statement: z is not a nonpositive integer
analytic_domains.label: DERIVED
analytic_domains.source: nonpositive integers have Re z <= 0, excluded by Re z>0

branch_conventions: the integrand is the continuous limit at t=0 of the written combination (removable singularity of 1/(1-e^{-t}))

derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: exp(-t)=1 iff t=0 for real t; t=0 is an endpoint, not an interior pole

why_not_cse_lgg: An integral against the Bose factor 1/(1-e^{-t}) is a named special-function representation of psi, not a common subexpression. LGG does not invent that kernel.
proposer_leak_risk: Source writes the integral and psi. Do not leak 'Bose occupation', 'Matsubara generating integral', or 'thermal master kernel' as gold names.
notes: Integral is not in PARSE_POLICY; this is a representation identity. Distinct from thermal-06 (Fermi-Dirac polylog 25.12.14-16) and from thermal-02 (Im psi = coth). T>0 is not imported: the source is Re z>0.
